### Kuwait & GCC Agricultural Support, Regulations, and Sector Performance The table below details state support programs, land allocation policies, financing mechanisms, regulatory frameworks, food import dependencies, and agricultural production statistics across Kuwait and the GCC, strictly based on confirmed source data: | Policy / Industry Category | Specific Metric / Provision Details | Governing Body / Regulatory Framework | Citation Grounding | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Agricultural Governance & Agency Roles** | • **PAAF / PAAFR:** Formulates agricultural/fishery policies, manages land grants, and disburses production subsidies.
• **KFAS:** Funds food security research and pilot indoor/vertical farming projects.
• **KISR:** Conducts applied R&D, technology transfer, sand drift control, and crop/water management.
• **Saudi ADF:** Governmental credit institution financing plant, animal, and fish production projects up to **SAR 20 Million (\$5.33 Million)** per project. | • Public Authority for Agriculture Affairs and Fish Resources (PAAFR) *(Kuwait)*
• Kuwait Foundation for the Advancement of Sciences (KFAS)
• Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research (KISR)
• Agricultural Development Fund (ADF) *(Saudi Arabia)* | [1-4] | | **Land Allocation & Plot Grants** | • **Al-Abdali Livestock Plots:** Allocated **500 land plots** (**50,000 m²** each) for meat/poultry production, plus **200 integrated farms** combining crops, sheep, fish, and poultry.
• **Dairy Cattle Holdings:** **50 larger plots** (**170,000 m²** each) allocated for cattle and milk production *(noted as being removed due to a railway route obstruction)*.
• **Total Farm Area:** **2,880 farms** encompassing **~141 million m²** (**14,100 ha**) across Al-Wafra, Al-Abdali, Al-Sulaibiya, and Kabd.
• **Arable Land Constraint:** Potentially usable land is **<1% to <9%** of total land area. | • PAAF / Ministry of State for Development and Sustainability *(Kuwait)*
• Land Tenure Act | [1, 2, 5, 6] | | **Land Tenure & Environmental Regulations** | • **Land Transfer Ban:** Strict directive prohibiting all forms of disposal, assignment, sale, partition, merging, or ownership transfer of allocated agricultural/fishery plots, pens, and nurseries.
• **Application Freeze:** Suspension of all new landholding applications and cancellation of previously registered pending applications.
• **EIA Requirement:** Environmental Management for Sustainable Act mandates a formal Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), social impact study, and project feasibility study for any land grant exceeding **2 hectares** (**20,000 m²**). | • PAAF Directive (*Kuwait Alyawm* Gazette)
• Ministry of State for Development & Sustainability
• Environmental Public Authority (KEPA) | [6-8] | | **Financial Loans & SME Support Programs** | • **Kuwait SME Fund:** Capitalized at **2 Billion KWD**; provides soft-debt financing up to **80%** of CapEx with a **≤2%** fee and a **1 to 3-year** grace period. Exempts equipment from custom duties/taxes and mandates retail space allocation in public co-operatives.
• **Saudi ADF Financing:** Approved **\$2 Billion** in loans in 2025; covers **70% to 75%** CapEx for high-tech agribusiness (greenhouses, aquaculture) and **60%** for external food security investments (10-year loan, 2-year grace); provides working capital loans covering 1–2 years. | • Kuwait National Fund for SME Development (Law E98/2013)
• Saudi Agricultural Development Fund (ADF) / Saudi Investment Bank (SAIB) | [3, 4, 9-11] | | **Direct Farm Subsidies & Fodder Rules** | • **Kuwait Annual Subsidies (\$30.6M Total, 2015–2016):** Fodder (**\$15.7M** / 51%), Plant production (**\$8.2M** / 27%), Milk/cows (**\$3.9M** / 12%), Date palms (**\$1.8M** / 6%), Fisheries (**\$0.5M** / 2%), Other (**\$0.5M** / 2%).
• **Livestock Eligibility Thresholds:** Subsidies restricted to holdings with at least **50 head of sheep/goats** or **15 head of camels/cattle**; horse subsidies discontinued.
• **Feed Formulation Rules:** Subsidized feed allotments must contain **≥50% mixed manufactured feed** (replacing unblended barley). | • PAAF Subsidy Framework
• Reform Decisions by Ministry of State for Development and Sustainability | [2, 7] | | **Water Infrastructure & Supply** | • **Groundwater Outtake:** **300,000 to 545,000 m³/day** extracted from brackish aquifers (TDS **1,300–7,000 ppm** / **3,000–10,000 mg/L**).
• **On-Farm Desalination:** Farmers utilize BWRO units to reduce salinity to 50–800 ppm at a levelized cost of **\$0.33 – \$0.48 / m³**.
• **Treated Sewage Effluent (TSE):** MPW treats municipal wastewater across 6 plants; **65%** of TSE is reused for agricultural/landscape irrigation at **\$0.28 / m³**.
• **Water Subsidy per m³:** **not in sources** | • Ministry of Electricity & Water (MEW)
• Ministry of Public Works (MPW) | [2, 6] | | **Food Import Dependence Figures** | • **Overall Regional Dependency:** GCC countries import **>70% to 90%** of food needs; GCC food import spending projected to reach **\$49 Billion** by 2020 (up from \$24B in 2008); Saudi food imports reached **\$10.3 Billion** in 2023.
• **Kuwait Self-Sufficiency Rates:** Overall fresh vegetables **51%** (49% imported); Onions **7%** (93% imported); Garlic **3%** (97% imported); Carrots **2%** (98% imported); Red meat **15%** (85% imported); Fish **9%–16%** (84%–91% imported; **23,285 tonnes** imported in 2012); Shrimp **19%** (81% imported); Grains (wheat, barley, corn) **<0.05%** (>99.95% imported).
• **Annual Net Import Tonnage (2017):** Potatoes **92,358 tonnes**; Tomatoes **57,473 tonnes**; Carrots **20,617 tonnes**; Green Peppers **19,371 tonnes**; Lettuce **17,178 tonnes**; Cabbage **10,051 tonnes**. | • PAAF Statistical Bulletin
• GCC Trade Statistics / WITS | [2, 5, 12] | | **Current Agriculture Production Numbers** | • **Cultivated Area:** **18,900 ha** (**189 km²**) total cropped land, or **121 km²** under vegetable cultivation.
• **Cultivation Types:** **85%** open field, **15%** protected field (of which 57% is uncooled plastic tunnels, 28% cooled plastic tunnels, 15% glass/fiberglass/acrylic greenhouses).
• **Economic Contribution:** Agriculture accounts for **0.53%** of GDP (2016) and employs **<1.1%** of the national workforce. Crops represent **56%** of gross agricultural production value; livestock represents **38%**.
• **Livestock Population (2013–2014):** **628,041** sheep (+41% over 2009–2010), **153,391** goats (+1%), **9,192** camels (+11%).
• **Fisheries & Aquaculture Output:** Capture fisheries yield **~4,500 tonnes/year**. Aquaculture projects include Al-Khiran floating cages (**2,000–3,000 tonnes/yr**), Boubyan Island (**3,000 tonnes** fish, **3,000 tonnes** shrimp), and Al-Sabia shrimp farm (**2,000 tonnes/yr**).
• **First Indoor Vertical Farm (2019):** **3,000 m²** growing area producing up to **550 kg/day** of leafy greens and herbs. | • Central Statistical Bureau (CSB)
• PAAF Annual Bulletin
• ITA Commercial Reports | [1, 2, 5] | --- ### Technical & Regulatory Summary Notes 1. **Governance & Regulatory Enforcement**: - Recent administrative reforms in Kuwait focus on eliminating speculative landholding and fiscal leaks [7, 8]. The complete ban on disposing of state-allocated agricultural land (published in *Kuwait Alyawm*) ensures plots cannot be transferred or sold privately [8]. - Non-compliant operations face immediate revocation of land rights and subsidy suspensions [7, 8]. 2. **Subsidies & Livestock Support Alignment**: - Feed support in Kuwait requires field verification of active production stock, enforcing strict minimum herd sizes (**50 sheep/goats**, **15 camels/cattle**) [7]. - Mandating that subsidized feed contain **at least 50% mixed manufactured feed** shifts animal nutrition away from unblended imported barley toward balanced rations, optimizing feed conversion and protecting strategic reserves [7]. 3. **Funding Mechanisms for High-Tech Agribusiness**: - Both Kuwait (via the National SME Fund) and Saudi Arabia (via the ADF) provide low-cost capital (**70%–80%** project financing) to lower CapEx barriers for closed-loop Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) [3, 4, 9]. - These frameworks incentivize automated greenhouses and vertical farming to overcome extreme climatic constraints and reduce reliance on external food imports [1, 4, 5, 9]. --- 💡 **Would you like me to prepare an executive brief or presentation outline on leveraging Kuwait SME Fund or Saudi ADF financing for setting up a commercial CEA facility?**

These tasks are: (Project documents) This study present tasks no 8 addressing the “Potential of Protected Agriculture and Hydroponics”. The objective of this task is to compare the productivity per unit of water and land of different fruit and vegetable crops in open field and under green house conditions (protected agriculture)., The study also consider the productivities of the — hydroponics-growing techniques in Qatar and other countries in the region with similar agroclimate conditions , based on the experience to date. The main outputs of this study are: a) water and land productivity of selected fruit and vegetable crops, including fodder under protected agriculture in Qatar calculated and compared with the same figure for open field; b) water productivity of selected fruit and vegetable crops, including fodder using soilless production techniques (hydroponics) in Qatar calculated and compared with production from soil based systems; c) Requirements of water, land and energy to produce different deficit crops, including fodder under greenhouse conditions using available hydroponics systems, considering different sophistication levels.
